name: Dividend Capture with Covered Call
summary: Hold shares through an ex-dividend date while short a call, collecting both the dividend and the premium - but only if the call is kept far enough OTM to avoid early exercise.

legs.strike_rule: shares held across the ex-dividend date
0.15-0.25 delta OTM, AND extrinsic value at the ex-date must exceed 1.5 x the declared dividend
legs.dte_rule: expiry at least 10 days AFTER the ex-dividend date

when_to_use: On dividend ETFs and blue chips where the system already wants the shares and the dividend is a meaningful part of total return. The whole art is avoiding early assignment on the day before ex-date.
typical_dte: expiry 20-45 days out, positioned so the ex-date is early in the option's life
entry_rules: Require the declared dividend, ex-date and pay-date from a reliable calendar; refuse to run this on an estimated dividend.

MANDATORY: option extrinsic value projected at the close of the day before ex-date must be >= 1.5 x the dividend per share. If not, the call will likely be exercised early. Compute extrinsic with a local BSM fit.
Choose an expiry at least 10 days after the ex-date so there is real extrinsic remaining.
Strike delta <= 0.25 - the further OTM, the safer from early exercise.
Shares must be held before the ex-date, not on it (T+1 settlement means buying ON the ex-date does not earn the dividend).
management_rules: Re-check extrinsic vs dividend at 15:00 ET on the day BEFORE the ex-date. If extrinsic < 1.10 x dividend, close or roll the call up-and-out immediately, before the close.
After the ex-date, manage the call normally at 50% profit / 21 DTE.
Expect a share price drop of approximately the dividend on the ex-date - this is not a loss and must not trigger the position stop; adjust the stop by the dividend amount.
exit_rules: HARD: close or roll the short call before the close on the day before ex-date whenever it is ITM or extrinsic < 1.10 x dividend. This is the single highest-probability early-assignment window in all of options trading.
Standard expiration guard: flatten ITM short calls by 15:30 ET on expiration day.
If assigned before the ex-date, the dividend is lost and the shares are gone - reconcile the ledger and stand down for the cycle.
assignment_risk: This is THE canonical early-assignment scenario: an ITM call whose remaining time value is less than the dividend will be exercised the day before the ex-date by any rational holder, because exercising captures the dividend and forfeits only the smaller extrinsic. The system must run an explicit dividend calendar and an extrinsic-vs-dividend comparison, not just a delta check.
liquidity_needs: Dividend-paying large caps and ETFs with liquid chains; OI >= 250.
common_mistakes: Writing a call whose extrinsic is smaller than the dividend and losing both the shares and the dividend; buying shares on the ex-date instead of before it; treating the ex-date price drop as a stop-loss trigger.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable; the dividend timeline is multi-day.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
